target:
def Target : Prop :=
  d15.D10 ∧ ¬ ∃ N : S1 Bool Bool, N.D9 ∧ S1.D6 N d15
a_raw: {"translation":"Target defines, but does not prove, the conjunction of two claims. First, there is a node of d15 with a nonempty directed chain of dependency steps back to itself. Since d15 has just one node, this amounts to a self-dependency. Second, there is no S1 system N with Boolean inputs and Boolean outputs such that both (i) for every node of N there is no nonempty dependency chain from that node back to itself, and (ii) for every finite Boolean input list, N and d15 give the same final output when each starts in its own initial state and processes the list from left to right. There is no length bound: d15 gives false on the empty list and gives true exactly on lists containing true. In either system, a dependency step from m to n means that there exist two global states and one Boolean input such that the states agree at every node other than m, but the updates at n on that same input differ. The witness states need not be reachable from the initial state. The comparison requires equality of outputs, not equality of nodes, state types, or internal states; N must have finitely many nodes, but its local state types need not be finite or Boolean."}
translation: Target defines, but does not prove, the conjunction of two claims. First, there is a node of d15 with a nonempty directed chain of dependency steps back to itself. Since d15 has just one node, this amounts to a self-dependency. Second, there is no S1 system N with Boolean inputs and Boolean outputs such that both (i) for every node of N there is no nonempty dependency chain from that node back to itself, and (ii) for every finite Boolean input list, N and d15 give the same final output when each starts in its own initial state and processes the list from left to right. There is no length bound: d15 gives false on the empty list and gives true exactly on lists containing true. In either system, a dependency step from m to n means that there exist two global states and one Boolean input such that the states agree at every node other than m, but the updates at n on that same input differ. The witness states need not be reachable from the initial state. The comparison requires equality of outputs, not equality of nodes, state types, or internal states; N must have finitely many nodes, but its local state types need not be finite or Boolean.

divergences.description: The cited passages do not specify a Boolean OR latch, its initial value of false, or the readout of its single bit. These are the author's choices of witness, not details of an example in either passage.

Lean gives “feedforward” a precise model not specified in P2: finitely many synchronously updated units with no cycle of effective state dependencies. Dependence is tested even on unreachable states, and the local state types and update functions need not be those of conventional neural units. The exclusion applies to every finite size, not to infinite networks.

judgement.summary: Under the stated unbounded-time reading, the target gives the claimed counterexample: a single true input remains visible after arbitrarily many false inputs without any change of update rule, and no one finite feedforward system matches its outputs on all finite lists. This makes the persistent trace observable at the output, rather than merely a difference in hidden state.
